label: input i at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter i during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 4 or later (t = 4..8). Fires on essentially every such step (about 3.4% of steps at each of orig_idx 4-8, which is the base rate of i). Never fires on i at positions 0-3, on any other token (a few dozen stray activations on other letters at most), on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, including when i is input or output there. Magnitude depends strongly on position: at t=4 it is weak (about 0.05-0.4 of max; 33% of activations but only 5% of mass), and it rises at t>=5, with the top activations (about 3.3) at t=8 in L=9 sequences. Previous tokens, first token, digit count and repeats have little effect, though first occurrences of i activate somewhat more than repeats.

issues: Minor only. The 103 missed activations on the test split are scattered across non-i tokens, mostly at step 8 of L=9 sequences, with relative magnitudes around 0.01-0.02 and about 0% of activation mass. This is noise, not a systematic gap.

There are 37 false positives, all i at t=4. This fits the explanation's point that t=4 activations are weak and sometimes drop below threshold. Coverage of the lowest activation quartile is still 0.99.

The profile confirms the factual claims. There are zero activations on the delimiter, in the copy phase, or at t<4. The firing rate is 0.034 at each orig_idx 4-8. t=4 accounts for 33% of activations but 5.1% of mass. Mass per activation is highest at t=8 and in L=9 sequences.
The label matches the predicate exactly, so it does not overclaim. Test scores: precision 0.999, recall 0.998, F1 0.998, mass recall 1.000.
